 Follow Severe thunderstorms could bring hail, damaging winds, tornado to NJ
 Amanda Oglesby, Asbury Park Press Updated Thu, November 12, 2026 at 5:34 PM UTC 1 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. Hail, thunderstorms and the chance of a tornado are possible Thursday, Nov. 12, as a low-pressure system moves across parts of central and southern New Jersey, according to the National Weather Service.
 Temperature differences between the system and a warm front could lead to the development of storm supercells, according to the National Weather Service's Storm Prediction Center. The storms could generate large hail and damaging winds as well as risk forming a tornado, according to the weather service.
 The low pressure system moving across New Jersey is strengthening through Thursday afternoon and could lead to fast-developing storms, said lead meteorologist Mike Lee at the Mount Holly station of the National Weather Service.
 People walk along the wind swept Manasquan boardwalk Friday morning, September 25, 2026. Warm, moist air on the ground in southern New Jersey and across the I-95 corridor combined with cold air in the upper atmosphere is fueling the storms, he said.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "Those storms will be able to develop at the surface and still rise through the atmosphere," Lee said. "We are expecting the worst of it to continue in the afternoon and maybe in the early evening hours."
 Shattered showers and some lingering thunder could continue through tonight, he said.
 More: Flash flood warning issued for Jersey Shore area 
 On Friday, temperatures will be colder with highs in the middle to upper 40s, he said. Temperatures Friday night into Saturday morning are likely to plunge into the upper 20s and lower 30s across much of New Jersey, he said.
